class_id: a regex corrupted by invisible control characters in the source
feature: any pattern written into a source file through a shell heredoc or generated edit (scraper/scripts/*.py, scripts/lib/*.mjs, and every future generated matcher)
symptom: an escape sequence is interpreted BEFORE the file is written, so the source holds the literal control byte instead of the two-character escape. A pattern written as backslash-b-EPS-backslash-b becomes BACKSPACE-EPS-BACKSPACE and can never match anything. Nothing reports an error: the file parses, the module imports, the function runs and returns a clean negative. Editors, terminals, diffs and file-reading tools all render the byte invisibly, so the code READS correctly on screen. The failure therefore presents as a LOGIC gap - the matcher looks not-clever-enough - and the search for it goes to the algorithm rather than the bytes.
first_seen: 2026-09-11, item 8a slice 3, and it was the THIRD occurrence in one night of the same underlying trap. Earlier the same night it made a mutation test silently no-op (the needle contained a backspace, matched nothing, and the suite stayed green - nearly recorded as 'the mutation survived, so the guard is hollow', a false conclusion about working code). Here it cost about thirty minutes: I checked the logic, then cleared __pycache__ suspecting stale bytecode, then compared module identity and globals, before finally printing the compiled code object's constants and seeing the backspace bytes.
fix_prs: #596 - the corrupted pattern repaired, and a test added that scans this slice's modules for control characters. Building such strings with chr(92) rather than writing a backslash through a heredoc is the prevention; the test is the detection for when prevention is forgotten, which it has been three times.
detection_check: scraper/scripts/test_peer_table_columns.py - test_no_source_file_contains_a_control_character scans every peer_table_* module for bytes below 0x09 or between 0x0b and 0x1f. Mutation-checked: injecting one real backspace into a regex turns it red by name. Scoped to this slice's own files deliberately - a check that reports on files its owner cannot fix is a check that gets switched off.
status: guarded for the item 8 modules only. Every other generated matcher in the repo is unguarded, and a repo-wide scan is the obvious extension - not taken here because it belongs to whoever owns the lint gate rather than to an item 8 slice.
